variants.name: old-growth
variants.note: a giant with a long clear trunk of thick, deeply furrowed bark and a narrow, ragged, flat-topped crown of heavy drooping limbs

description: A very tall, straight conifer, 30-60 m high, with soft flat needles all round the twigs, branches that droop and then lift at the tips, and thick, deeply furrowed red-brown bark on old trees. Here it grows above about 600 m on cool north slopes and in canyons with ponderosa pine and incense cedar, and its hanging cones have three-pointed bracts sticking out between the scales, like the back legs and tail of a mouse hiding inside.

season_notes.winter: Evergreen: the needles stay on for five to eight years, and last year's cones hang empty in the upper crown.
season_notes.spring: Bright yellow-green new shoots burst from papery bud scales at every branch tip (April-June), and small red seed cones and yellow pollen cones appear.
season_notes.summer: The new shoots darken to the old needles' colour while the hanging cones swell, green at first, then brown.
season_notes.fall: Ripe cones open and drop winged seeds (September-October); chickarees and chipmunks cut and store the cones.

notes: Douglas-fir in the central Sierra Nevada is the coastal variety (var. menziesii), at the southern end of its Sierra range (it thins out south of Yosemite). Around Placerville and Shingle Springs it is at its lower edge: above about 600 m, on cool north-facing slopes and in canyons, with ponderosa pine, incense cedar, black oak and canyon live oak; not on the hot south slopes of the oak woodland. 30-60 m in the Sierra mixed conifer forest, here 30-48 m in the file with an old-growth class to 60 m, dbh to 1.5 m (radius_ratio 0.022). Strongly excurrent (length_ratio 1, taper 1). Architectural model: monopodial orthotropic trunk with rhythmic whorls of plagiotropic branches carrying flat sprays, Massart's model (provisional; some authors put Pseudotsuga under Rauh's). Branches in whorls of three to five plus smaller ones between (whorl 4, 40 limbs), the upper ones ascending, the middle roughly level, the lower ones drooping and turning up at the tips (droop_deg 30, upturn_deg 25), with pendent side shoots (level-2 tropism -0.1, droop 15, twig tropism -0.2): the drooping branch tips. Young trees are dense, symmetrical spires to the ground (young class, smooth grey bark with resin blisters: bark_pattern smooth); mature trees in stands lose their lower limbs (base 0.3, dead lower limbs 18%, branch stubs on the bole); old trees have a long clear bole, a narrow, ragged, often flat top and very thick (10-30 cm), corky, deeply furrowed dark red-brown bark (furrowed, ridge 10 cm, fissure 0.85). Needles 2-3 cm, flat, soft, blunt, spirally set but twisted into two ranks along the side shoots, dark yellow-green to blue-green: leaf_shape needle_flat, leaf_size_m 0.025, one plane per card (the sprays are flat; twist_deg turns them about the shoot for volume), hanging (tuft_up 0, droop 0.4). Spring flush bright yellow-green (spring colour and a light palette tint). Cones 5-10 cm, pendulous, in the upper crown, with three-pointed bracts sticking out between the scales; they are part of needle_flat's look if the generator draws them, and no cone field is set here. Colour from the photographs (r/g 0.91, b/g 0.61). Not an oak: no acorns.
sources: Hermann and Lavender 1990, Silvics of North America vol. 1, Pseudotsuga menziesii
